The primary material of a candle is wax, typically derived from paraffin, beeswax, or soy, which serves as the fuel source that burns to produce light.

Regarding the provided text, the primary theme is the contrast in how two literary works handle the concept of good versus evil. The similarity in presentation lies in the fact that both J.R.R. Tolkien's 'The Lord of the Rings' and C.S. Lewis's 'The Chronicles of Narnia' share the prevalent theme of good versus evil. The difference in presentation is found in the complexity of their moral landscapes: 'The Lord of the Rings' offers a clear distinction between forces of good and darkness, whereas 'The Chronicles of Narnia' blurs this line by introducing characters who waver between sides, resulting in a more nuanced view of morality.
